title: Drift in a single year: up and down
objectives: Read the single-year drift table both ways.
State how much money moves in each case.
body_md:
Same ₹20 L, 60/40 starting portfolio. Illustrative.

| After a year when… | Equity share becomes | Rebalancing means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Equity +30%, debt +7% | ≈ 65% | Move about ₹1.1 L from equity to debt |
| Equity −25%, debt +7% | ≈ 51% | Move about ₹1.5 L from debt to equity |
example: Equity +30%, debt +7% → ≈ 65% equity, move about ₹1.1 L from equity to debt. Equity −25%, debt +7% → ≈ 51% equity, move about ₹1.5 L from debt to equity.
say: After a strong year, rebalancing sells equity.
After a fall, rebalancing buys equity.
never: A fall means selling more equity.

check.q: The main job of rebalancing is…
check.why: Risk control. It keeps risk at the agreed level.

check.q: After equity +30% and debt +7%, a 60/40 portfolio is about:
check.why: After a year when equity +30%, debt +7%: equity share becomes ≈ 65%.

check.q: After equity −25% and debt +7%, rebalancing means:
o: Moving about ₹1.5 L from debt to equity
check.why: Equity −25%, debt +7%: ≈ 51%; rebalancing means moving about ₹1.5 L from debt to equity.
